From: Myers, Gene <gmyers@freepress.com>
Sent: Thursday, October 23, 2014 1:54 AM
To: Birkett, David <dbirkett@freepress.com>; Brudenell, Mike <mbrudenell@freepress.com>; Bull, Kevin <kbull@freepress.com>; Collison, Bill <bcollison@freepress.com>; Crawford, Kirkland <kcrawford@freepress.com>; Darby, David <dfdarby@freepress.com>; delaGarza, Marisela <mdelagarza@freepress.com>; Delves, Laurie <ldelves@freepress.com>; Ellis, Vince <vellis@freepress.com>; Farrell, Perry <pafarrell@freepress.com>; Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>; Ford, Ryan <rford@freepress.com>; Jahnke, James <jjahnke@freepress.com>; Lowe, John <jlowe@freepress.com>; Manzullo, Brian <bmanzullo@freepress.com>; Marcinkoski, Tim <tmarcinkoski@freepress.com>; McCabe, Mick <mmccabe@freepress.com>; Monarrez, Carlos <cmonarrez@freepress.com>; Rexrode, Joe <jrexrode@freepress.com>; St. James, Helene <hstjames@freepress.com>; Schrader, Steve <sschrader@freepress.com>; Sharp, Drew <dsharp@freepress.com>; Seidel, Jeff <jseidel@freepress.com>; Sipple, George <gsipple@freepress.com>; Snider, Lee <lsnider@freepress.com>; Snyder, Mark <msnyder@freepress.com>; Tarsha, Jeff <jtarsha@freepress.com>; Visconti, Joy <jvisconti@freepress.com>; Weber, Jessica <jweber@freepress.com>; Windsor, Shawn <swindsor@freepress.com>; Myers, Gene <gmyers@freepress.com>
Cc: Gene Myers <myersgene@comcast.net>; Beth Myers (myersbg@comcast.net) <myersbg@comcast.net>
Subject: THURSDAY-FOR-FRIDAY 
 
Gene here with the early line on the Thursday plan …
A couple of important notes (including immediate action for folks who will move):
1) OK … here’s the sparse vacation lineup for this week: John (until late October – and then off into the Texas sunset).
2) Kevin will be the day editor, arriving in the morning. He will be ably assisted by Mari starting at 3:30 p.m. David has Preps Extra duties.
3) As for yours truly, I will arrive in the late morning. Might exit stage left late in the afternoon for fun activity. Or might not.

4) Ol’ Seamhead Update I: I was sitting right next to John in his Dearborn apartment – conducting a debriefing – when Joe Buck (and then his Fox partners) gave a late-inning shout-out to our retiring Seamhead. WITH THE SOUND MUTED. At 11:09 p.m., my phone buzzed with this text from Kevin: Shoutout! I didn’t understand. A few seconds later my phone buzzed again with this text from Anthony: Did you hear that? Joe Buck just gave John a shout-out. Fortunately, John’s TV – which was on the floor because he had donated its fancy-pants stand to the Salvation Army earlier in the day – had replay capability. He was smiling ear-to-ear as we heard the comments from Buck, Verducci and Reynolds. And then BOTH John’s iPhones started exploding.

5) Ol’ Seamhead Update II: What led Buck to makes his comments? He could have been prodded by his sideline reporter, Ken Rosenthal, one of John’s best friends in the business. Or he might have been prodded by Jon Paul Morosi, who had been prodded the previous night by Jo-Ann Barnas. At her suggestion, Jon tried to get word to the Fox producer to pass the word to Buck. I like this theory best because it’s two Free Press alums working in cahoots. Also, Buck’s shout-out said John had announced his retirement “today” – which would have been true, of course, Tuesday, not Wednesday.

6) Ol’ Seamhead Update III: James put together a little story and a collection of tweets about John. Here’s the link. http://www.freep.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2014/10/22/john-lowe-detroit-tigers/17716415/ Also, plug “John Lowe” into Twitter to see all the great things folks are writing. My favorite:
Andy McCullough ‏@McCulloughStar 9h9 hours ago
Not since A-Rod in 2007 has a person hijacked attention during the World Series like John Lowe. Farewell and good luck to a nice man.

7) Ol’ Seamhead Update IV: Rosenthal also wrote a 12-paragraph blog on John. My favorite part: “I can only hope the Baseball Writers Association of America votes John its highest honor, the J.G. Taylor Spink Award, for meritorious contributions to baseball writing. Rarely will it be more deserved.”
8) How ’bout those Royals! Forget “momentum is tomorrow’s starting pitcher.” This year it’s “momentum is tomorrow’s sixth-, seventh-, eighth- and ninth-inning bullpen.”
9) Here’s the web lineup: Webmizz at 5 a.m., James at 8 a.m., Brian at 1:30 p.m. and Anthony at 8 p.m.
10) For Friday’s print editions, our space is plentiful but tight. So if you have an extra story, please alert Kevin ASAP.
11) Time for the VITAL, URGENT and UPDATED housekeeping reminders …
12) Only two days until we move. Do you know where you junk is? Find it … and toss it.

13) PRIORITY NO. 1 ON THURSDAY: Look at the first two photo attachments. Find this sheet of paper in your moving packet. Fill out the back – and put it on Laurie’s desk immediately. Or sooner. If you don’t, you crate could end up in Omaha.
14) Wednesday was the official deadline to pack your crate and dispose of trash, recycling and items not moving. Your final critical items must be crated by Friday.
15) For reporters … you need your mailboxes cleaned out by Thursday night. Anything not claimed by Friday morning will be thrown away! (Unless we can make a profit off it on eBay.)

16) THE MOST IMPORTANT REMINDER: Now … to clear up some conflicting information you may have heard about how we will depart from one building and arrive in our new home. Michigan.com (new name for the old DMP) wants folks out of the building (to never return) by NOON FRIDAY. However, that will not work for the Sports Department, for obvious reasons. We will produce the Friday-for-Saturday digital and print products and the Saturday-for-Sunday digital and products in our old building. We will produce the Sunday-for-Monday digital (mostly) and print products in our new building. HOWEVER, IF YOU ARE NOT SCHEDULED FOR A COPY EDITING SHIFT OR NAMED MOVING CAPTAIN LAURIE … YOU CANNOT BE IN THE BUILDING AFTER NOON FRIDAY AND YOU CANNOT ENTER THE NEW BUILDING UNTIL MONDAY MORNING! Around 11:59 p.m. Saturday, AJ and Steve will start to unhook computers and our department will be moved down the street during the overnight hours. AJ and Steve hope to have us up and running in our new home by 1 p.m. Sunday. (Because of this and the Lions’ early game in London, Brian will work his 7 a.m. web shift remotely and Steve will start his Lions shift in lovely Livonia.) Anthony, working the overnight web shift, will be the last to leave Friday night. I will be the last to leave Saturday night. (Kirkland will do the overnight web shift from his Florida lair.) Anthony will be the first to arrive Sunday afternoon. Laurie will be the first to arrive Monday morning, followed by James.

17) TO KEEP YOU OUT OF TROUBLE REMINDER: To reiterate a note from Grace: “As a reminder, no furniture of any kind is to leave the building (chairs, bookcases, file cabinets, coat racks, tables, shelving units, TVs, etc.).  If there is a piece of furniture (or something that resembles furniture) that personally belongs to you, you must have a pass to remove it from the building. See Grace Bennett for a pass.”

18) This is for those of us who work outside the office. You probably saw this e-mail Wednesday evening from Jody Williams: Please see posting by Paul on the Insider. At the bottom of this file, I will include Paul’s e-mail, which is pretty long.

19) For today’s attached photo … Virgin Atlantic, via FedEx priority morning delivery, sent Kevin a bizarre care packet to celebrate expanded service to Metro and the Lions playing in England. The package included fresh pot pies, sausage rolls and other meaty products. If  you want to risk it, they are in the fridge. The package also included Digestives – chocolate-coated wafers that looked pretty darn good – but I would rather eat the possibly tainted meat than something with such an unappetizing name.
Showrunners: Kevin (late morning), Mari (3:30).
Websters: Webmizz morning (5:00), James morning (8:00), Brian day (1:30), Anthony night (8:00).
Designer:  Ryan (3:30).
Yours truly:  The Moose still is loose!
Notes: David will work on Preps Extra.
Your text assignments (some ending in 1024) should have arrived Wednesday night from Jessica.
As always, we’re in the market for news.
JEFF

DAVE

Did I forget anything?
Gene
PAUL’S NOTE TO THE STAFF!!!

Folks,This fall, we'll be taking more transformational steps to laser-focus the Free Press newsroom on our digital priorities.
 
First, we'll be doing more staff training on metrics -- details to come soon -- and how to plan content for different platforms and  audiences. How to analyze traffic, maximize it, learn from what performs well and what doesn't. We need to emphasize, more and more, reaching readers in the 25-45 age demographic.We've done significant training already, but we'll be taking it to another level. All of us will participate.
 
But let's be clear -- great traffic and reader interaction start with great content.That's what we're all about: Watchdog reporting. Information that informs uniquely, entertains and surprises. Story-telling as only we can do it here. Commentary that emphasizes our leadership role in Michigan. Compelling presentation and visuals on all platforms, print and digital.
 
And we know that the Free Press has always been known for creativity -- doing the darnedest things. Putting on our own TV show. Putting a mayor in jail. Explaining How Detroit Went Broke. Starting the Freep Film Fest. Doing national ground-breaking work on charter schools and how Michigan's governance is mightily flawed.I could go on and on. So could you. We will continue to do that kind of work.But we can never be satisfied. We have to move to the future. We must keep on this road of digital transformation, and accelerate. 
 
With that in mind, we will be working over the next few weeks on our newsroom structure.We will be changing some job descriptions, creating some new positions, organizing around digital priorities, keeping our content strong and enriching it, streamlining how our content gets posted.We'll be looking at how our managers and staff are structured, and many manager titles and job descriptions will   change to help underscore our transformation and to allow us to do more special projects, more innovative work, more new products and initiatives. We have a lot of work ahead of us this fall.As a first step in reorganizing, I'm pleased to announce some talented top managers moving into new positions, effective Nov. 3:Nan Laughlin will become Managing Director. She will report to me and be responsible for newsroom operations and content on all platforms. She'll bring her dynamic editing and energy to bear across the newsroom, with special emphasis on expanding our news and business reporting -- including enterprise and investigative.Robert Huschka will become Managing Director/Customer Experience. He will report to me and will apply his multi-platform savvy and ability to quickly analyze content to great effect. He'll make sure we deliver customized content at the right time on the right platform for the right audience. He'll oversee the web desk and central Hub, plus our copy editing and design teams.Stephen Henderson will become Managing Director of Opinion and Community Engagement. Steve will report to me, continue to be responsible for A Better Michigan content and will take a more active role in the newsroom. He'll participate in long-range brainstorming and planning of enterprise -- so we can even better capitalize on his knowledge of the community, sources and deep skills (think Pulitzer Prize).Nancy Andrews will become Chief of Innovation, a new concept that will put Nancy at the forefront of change in the newsroom. She will report to me and look for ways to innovate (think Freep TV show) and generate new products, working with us and colleagues at Michigan.com. She'll continue to oversee photo-video, lead special training (think Turbo Video), and will direct selected special Free Press projects, emphasizing digital (think How Detroit Went Broke). Nancy will have a small creative team reporting to her -- details to come -- and will call on expertise through the newsroom for projects as appropriate.Julie Topping will become Senior Director of Content Strategy. She will report to Nan, work closely with her on newsroom content strategy and apply her ample creative talents (think MiBestLife projects, special sections) and thoughtful approach especially to quality-of-life coverage in all forms, from sports to entertainment to features. That coverage will be enhanced with deeper enterprise, story-telling and watchdog as well.Ashley Woods will become Director of Audience Analysis. She will report to Robert and work with not only the web desk and Hub but across the newsroom. Ashley has made quite an impact here, and she'll be involved in training and hands-on coaching to help departments, teams and individual staff members plan and execute content so it's seen by the most readers possible as grow traffic.Please know how excited I am to have these talented folks in these new roles. They and other key managers make up an incredible team. And I want to add this:I'm proud of the work we're doing, the way we have responded to what life throws at us, the way we've adapted ourselves to Presto and gotten ourselves ready to move into new offices. For that, we owe a special debt to A.J. Hartley and Grace Bennett.   
 
We will have more announcements soon -- on the next round of training, on more changing management titles and responsibilities through the organization, on some reporting positions with new job descriptions.We're all in this transformation together, and we're going to come out the other side well equipped to succeed going forward.
 
  --Paul
